intro: This section is the layer that was missing. The steps of each process are already documented — HIMS_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md §4.A–§4.G walk them screen by screen, and §8 traces one end-to-end worked example. What follows is the architecture above those steps: the process taxonomy, who owns each process, where control passes between roles, and the invariants that hold across all of them.

The organising idea is that this module runs one long-running loop per employee — assess, identify a gap, close it, verify the closure, feed the result back into the next assessment — with three supporting cycles (credential renewal, succession, recognition) hanging off it at different frequencies.
landscapeCaption: Figure 5.1 — Process landscape. The four value-chain processes run left to right; the four supporting processes cut across all of them. An arrow is a handover of control, not a data copy.

taxonomy.intro: Level 0 is the value chain. Level 1 is a process with a single accountable owner. Level 2 is the procedure a user carries out, and it is at Level 2 that the existing documentation takes over.

items.trigger: Reporting line cannot supply a reviewer
New role, standard or accreditation change
On demand from the gap screens
Gap pattern or new course offering

swimlaneCaption: Figure 5.2 — Performance review, as a control-handover diagram. Each vertical band is a role; each box is a step that role owns exclusively. The two dashed gates are enforced by derived state, not by a stored status column or a scheduled job.

handovers.intro: The architecturally interesting part of this module is not the steps — it is the points where control passes and cannot pass back. Each of these is enforced in code, not by convention.
rows: A review cannot be created in a cycle that has already ended, so a review is never born frozen.
Response submission unlocks only on finished. The reviewer keeps score authority throughout.
Editability is derived from end_date on every read, so the freeze holds even where no scheduler runs. Completed is nobody's to set by hand.
Acknowledgement locks the response permanently; the two timestamps are stored separately so the sequence is provable.
Nobody self-certifies. Completion is a statement about a person, so it needs the record-completion gate and a direct-report relationship; reopening is narrower still because it withdraws evidence.
Only verified hours count. Verification lands days after the log, which is why attained hours are summed on read rather than stored on the cycle.
Check-in is a session's only completion mechanism, so one fact never has two writers.
A supervisor can develop a candidate without seeing the ratings that placed them: scores, 9-box label, readiness, mentor and status are redacted downward.

invariants.intro: Six rules hold across every process above. They are the reason the module behaves consistently rather than per-screen, and each one exists because its absence caused a real defect.

items.title: State that depends on a date is derived, never stored
items.body: Credential expiry, cycle closure and review editability are all computed on read from a date column. There is no nightly job to set them, because an authorisation rule that depends on schedule:run being wired is one that fails open on any box where it is not. The cost is that performance_reviews.status only ever holds draft or finished — so any query wanting "open reviews" must join the cycle, and a filter on the column alone silently misses the third state.

items.title: The clock is the hospital's clock
items.body: All three helpers ask "has this date passed?" against now(). Under the stock UTC default that question answered no for the first eight hours of every Philippine day — a cycle that ended yesterday stayed scoreable until 8am. Asia/Manila is therefore an authorisation setting, and a test pins it.

items.title: One fact, one writer
items.body: Course completion has exactly one write path and sessions have a different one, so no fact is recorded in two places. Overdue has one definition, in the service, and the dashboard calls it rather than counting again — a second copy would be free to drift the first time either changed.

items.title: Authority is identity, not role
items.body: Reviewer legitimacy is the reporting line. Admin and HR have no blanket review access and reach outside the chain only through a logged exception on one of four bases. These checks are private controller methods rather than Gates, because a Gate closure receives only the user — and every rule here needs the review row.

items.title: Visibility is the reporting line, not the department
items.body: scopeToVisibleEmployees() filters on supervisor_id. The rewrite changed behaviour in every module that calls it, which is why a test whose subject merely shares a department with the actor is now the negative case.

items.title: Compliance governs people, not accounts
items.body: Every compliance and notification path keys off employees.employee_id. An employee tracked by proxy — no login at all — is still assigned, still measured, still escalated about. That is the point, and the account-coverage report exists to name them.

aiProcess.intro: One process deserves separate treatment because it is the only one where a user's sentence becomes a database write. It is documented step-by-step in HIMS_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md §5.1; what matters architecturally is the order of the stages.

stages.name: Verb pre-filter
stages.note: Cheap rejection of anything that is plainly a question, before a model is involved.

stages.name: Planner
stages.note: Classifies the sentence to one of the catalogue's actions.

stages.name: Registry role check
stages.note: Before resolution. The catalogue's 30 entries derive their permission from the route's own middleware, so the assistant cannot outrank the UI.

stages.name: Entity resolver
stages.note: Names become UUIDs by lookup, not by generation.

stages.name: Executor
stages.note: Prefills and invokes the real controller — the same validation and the same authorisation the form would have hit.

stages.name: Audit
stages.note: The write is recorded as an AI action, with the actor still attributable.

aiProcess.closing: The role check sitting at stage 3 rather than stage 5 is the load-bearing detail: an unauthorised plan is refused before any entity is looked up, so the pipeline never confirms the existence of a record the caller may not see.
